title: Cheese and Marmite scones
subtitle: Savoury scones with sharp cheddar and a layer of Marmite baked through the dough
excerpt: These are savoury scones built around the pairing of sharp cheddar and Marmite. The Marmite is stirred directly into the liquid before mixing, which distributes it through the dough and gives every bite a deep, yeasty savouriness. Eat warm from the oven with cold butter.
sourceNotes: Marmite was introduced in the UK in 1902 and became a standard flavouring in British savoury baking. The combination of Marmite and cheddar in scones is well-documented in British home-baking literature from the late twentieth century onwards.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked scones and reheat at 180 degrees Celsius for 10 minutes from frozen.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and freeze half. The dough does not improve on resting; bake immediately.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day of baking. Scones are at their worst after 24 hours at room temperature; freeze if not eating immediately.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 220 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 200 degrees Celsius. Scones need a hot oven to rise fast before the butter melts completely.

glossaryTerms.definition: The single most common error in scone-making. Scone dough must be mixed until it just comes together and no further; the butter must stay in visible, irregular pieces and not be rubbed into fine crumbs. Overworked scone dough develops gluten, which makes the finished scones tough and prevents them rising cleanly along the sides.

. Stop mixing the moment the dough comes together and avoid the urge to knead it smooth.
Preheat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius. Line a baking tray with baking paper.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Add the cold cubed butter and work it in briefly with your fingertips until the mixture has irregular pea-sized lumps of butter throughout; do not rub it in to fine crumbs.

Stir the Marmite into the cold milk until fully dissolved. Add the grated cheddar to the flour mixture, then pour in the Marmite milk. Mix with a fork or palette knife until the dough just comes together; it should look rough and slightly sticky.
Tip onto a lightly floured surface and press gently into a 3 cm thick round. Cut out rounds with a 6 cm cutter by pressing straight down without twisting. Re-press any scraps once only.

Place on the prepared tray. Brush the tops with a little extra milk and scatter with the reserved cheddar. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and deep golden. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.
